the effects of early life nutrition on adult ovarian function and the potential for improving ovulation rate in Merino ewes.
the effect of early life nutrition on the adult ovary and the effect of short-term supplementation on ovarian function.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nutrition of the ewe during the pre-/perinatal period affects the ovulation rate of her adult offspring, but not the dynamics of follicular growth and atresia, or the responsiveness to a short-term supplement.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

early life nutrition and short-term supplementation with a high-quality protein feed (lupin) have additive effects on ovulation rate in Merino ewes, with no adverse effects on ovarian follicle dynamics.

the nutritional history of a ewe, and the supplementation of a ewe during the breeding season, affect the number of ovulations, and the number of granulosal cells and E2 concentrations in the dominant follicle, and these effects are mediated through changes in glucose and insulin concentrations.
nutrition in pre- and post-natally influences the reproductive performance of ewes, but the effects are not as dramatic as those seen in pre-pubertal ewe lambs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early nutrition has long-lasting effects on ovarian function and reproductive performance in ewes.
the nutritional environment in early life affects the ovarian response to short-term nutritional supplementation in adult ewes.
the nutrition of the mother in early life affects the ovarian function in the offspring and that this can be modified by supplementation in adult life.
